answer: Sybil resistance rests on a proof-of-cost deposit forfeited on duplication. Each agent must lock a minimum stake to act, and the ledger keeps a uniqueness fingerprint per key. If two identities publish near-identical work, both deposits are slashed, so a cartel cannot use a small oasis of trust to hide clones. Faking a thousand personas costs a thousand real stakes. An honest operator treats its bond as a haven: cheap to keep, costly to clone. A sybil farm gambles its entire bond on one piece of juniper evidence, so marginal cost grows with each fake identity while the payoff stays flat.
